correctness.rationale: All-stage analytical proof uses explicit complete multipartite Laplacian orthogonal projections, a coefficientwise nonnegative derivative numerator for E_s/O_s proving strictly decreasing f_s, and an exact integration-by-parts Padé error identity proving even-stage r_s>0. Odd-stage leading-coefficient limit gives 2J/N-I and the complete two-state exception follows from |r_s|<1. Assumptions, endpoints h=0, singleton parts, coinciding eigenvalues and s=1 are handled. An independently re-run exact symbolic/rational checker gives 741 assertions across stages 1..28 and finite graph cases; finite tests are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-positive-step parity classification for every stage s and all complete multipartite part-size profiles is not implied by the inspected published Gauss stability analysis or the positive-systems Padé restrictions. Related narrower statements treat explicit RK4 or only two-stage Gauss and smaller graph subclasses, none implies higher even-stage all-step positivity or odd-stage eventual diagonal loss for arbitrary class sizes. The claim is an identifiable structural extension with residual specialist-literature risk, not a declaration of universal priority.

value.rationale: This provides a complete and structurally explained high-order endpoint maximum-principle classification for the natural family of complete multipartite heat networks, including arbitrarily unbalanced stars. It separates every even-order Gauss collocation method from every odd-stage counterpart despite their shared A-stability, and differentiates these networks from arbitrary finite Markov chains where Padé positivity can fail. The all-order theorem gives an exact benchmark for geometric numerical positivity, not just a small instance or a generic corollary.
